security_problem: The identity-aware path is proven to deny inside the decision path and never proven at the backend. Six tests in internal/proxy/verified_actor_test.go assert that the proxy returned a denial; none of them proves the MCP server never received the call. H50's own text admits the limit: deny-before-relay at the intercept gate, not host/network isolation or an independent backend observer. A denial returned to the client for a call that was already relayed would satisfy every existing test and still be a complete failure of the property the project claims.
required_behavior: One canonical harness entry point (harness/identity-aware.sh, which runs tests/integration/verified_actor_harness_test.go with -count=1 -v) starts a mock MCP backend and a visor serve process configured with settings.require_verified_actor, drives the positive and negative scenario tables of the design contract, and asserts the exit criterion server_received(action) IMPLIES verified_actor(action) AND policy_allowed(action) AND durable_allow(action) from the backend observer's own artifact. The observer is a mock backend that appends one JSON line per received tools/call, recording received_at, transaction, method, tool and a hash of the raw arguments, to a file it owns outside the repository (a temp directory), and it must not import internal/audit or read visor's ledger: its only inputs are the bytes it receives on the wire. For every negative scenario the test asserts observer_received == false from that artifact, correlated by transaction id and never by ordering alone; for at least one positive scenario it asserts the artifact exists and is non-empty, so a missing artifact fails the test rather than passing it by omission. A discriminating control proves the negatives come from the gate: with settings.require_verified_actor absent, the same call carries no context and the observer receives it. harness/identity-aware.sh copies the observer artifact into evidence/harness/<timestamp>/identity-aware/ (an excluded evidence tree, so the recorded snapshot digest is unchanged by the run) and the repository never receives the observer log at any other path. harness/invariants.md gains one new row mapping each H52 property to the exact test that proves it and to the observer artifact field that proves it; the H50 row is not edited, widened or re-scoped.
failure_behavior: Every negative scenario fails the test if the observer recorded the call, if the denial is not produced, or if the artifact cannot be read; a missing or unreadable observer artifact is a failure, never a pass by omission. A scenario that cannot distinguish a gate denial from an unrelated failure fails the test, because the discriminating control must forward the same call when the identity requirement is absent. harness/identity-aware.sh exits non-zero when the test fails and does not write the artifact anywhere inside the digest-tracked tree.
non_goals: No enforcement change: this adds proof, it does not change the gate, its decisions or its reasons
Do not edit, widen, weaken or re-scope H50 or any existing invariant row
No compose stack, network topology or direct-bypass tests (separate card)
No evidence-correlation work across stable shared IDs (separate card)
No new capability-token format, no new policy schema, no new CLI flag for the proxy
No LLM, scoring, or model-generated claim anywhere in the decision or verification path
No host filesystem or network confinement
No dashboard or web control plane
No merge of mcp-visor with the identity-plane repository
